text:
emma: Quick sync: noticed hotspots from large-embed jobs causing noisy compaction and repeated full-page pins. Idea: expose fractional pinning (pin a portion of a large slab) + reclaim-hints so compactor/evictor can prefer low-impact regions. Thoughts?

rafael: Nice. Fractional pinning reduces tail latency for small slices but complicates residency accounting. How do we represent a fractional pin to the allocator?

priya: Keep residency counters at granularity G (e.g., 4KB) and allow pins to mark ranges with a fractional weight in (0,1] that reduces eviction priority proportionally. So eviction_score = base_score * (1 - pin_weight) for that range. Full pin still sets pin_weight=1.

emma: That avoids global refcount changes. We need an efficient wire format for reclaim-hints so offload workers can coalesce adjacent low-weight regions. Proposal: reclaim-hint = [(offset, length, weight), ...] attached to allocation completion and periodically updated.

rafael: Two concerns: 1) bookkeeping overhead and 2) fragmentation: fractional pins could make compaction less effective if many tiny weighted segments. Maybe quantize weight levels to a small set {0,0.25,0.5,0.75,1} and coalesce by (offset>>S) buckets.

priya: Agree quantize helps. Also add a policy: compactor treats weight<=0.25 as reclaimable and weight>=0.75 as protected. Middle weights are low-priority reclaimable with cost score. That gives a spectrum without micromanagement.

emma: How does this interact with offload and host-fallback? If we mark a region partially pinned, offloader should avoid spilling protected parts but can spill reclaimable fractions. We'll need atomic moves where only unprotected fractions are migrated.

rafael: Implementation sketch: maintain per-slab bitmap of bucketed weights + occupancy. Evictor scans prefer slots with low weight buckets. When offloading, we build a scatter list of reclaimable runs up to target bytes and migrate them. Must ensure correctness for in-flight K/V caches — use a small barrier: mark migrating region as in-flight, drain references, then flip backing.

priya: For performance, we should sample reclaim-hints instead of materializing full lists. Hints include an estimated reclaimable_bytes in last T seconds so evictor can preselect slabs. Detailed runs only computed on candidate slabs.

emma: Telemetry: emit fractional_pin_histogram, reclaim_hint_success_rate, compaction_reclaim_bytes_by_weight. We also need an admin toggle to disable fractional mode for Dedicated customers who want deterministic behavior.

rafael: Tests: unit tests for scoring, integration with compactor verifying compaction density improves for mixed workloads, and chaos tests with concurrent migrate+alloc to catch races. Also microbench popcount/bitmap ops to ensure scanning cost is acceptable.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: feature-branch fractional-pin-195 CI passed; canary started :rocket:

priya: Great. I'll write a short RFC describing the weight quantization, eviction_score formula, and migration protocol. Emma, can you prototype reclaim-hints API?

emma: Yep, will put up PR with API + small simul bench.
